verses.59:3: Deus, vós nos {rep1}, e nos destruístes: * vos irastes, e tivestes piedade de nós.
verses.59:4: Abalastes a terra, e a perturbastes: * curai as suas {contritiones}, porque {commota}.
verses.59:5: Mostrastes ao vosso povo coisas duras: * destes-nos a beber vinho de {compunctio}.
verses.59:6: Destes aos que vos temem um sinal: * para que fujam {afacie} arco:
verses.59:7: Para que sejam livrados os vossos amados: * {salvumfac} com a vossa direita, e escutai-me.
verses.59:8: Deus falou {insancto}: * eu me alegrarei, e repartirei Siquém: e medirei {convallem}.
verses.59:9: Meu é Galaad, e meu é Manassés: * e Efraim é a força da minha cabeça.
verses.59:10: {inidumaeam} estenderei o meu {calceamentum}: * a mim {subditi} os estrangeiros.
verses.59:11: Quem me {ded1} à cidade fortificada? * quem me {ded2} até a Idumeia?
verses.59:12: {nonne}, Deus, que nos {rep2}? * e não saireis, Deus, com as nossas forças?
verses.59:13: Dai-nos auxílio {detrib}: * porque é vã a salvação do homem.
verses.59:14: Em Deus {facvirt}: * e ele mesmo reduzirá a nada os que nos atribulam.

decisions.why: *repéllere* without *a* → *repelir* is settled (D42; the row names 59:3 and 59:12). The verb opens the psalm and returns in 59:12 as the name of the God who must lead the army (*qui repulísti nos*), so the two must be one word, and they are. The row warns that the Ps 42 blind reader did not know *repelistes*; the blind reader of this psalm is the second test. DRB 'cast off'; MS1932 *desamparaste* (another verb: derelínquere's field).

options.label: rejeitastes
options.note: plainer to the ear, but *rejeitar* is reprobáre's (117:22).

options.label: desamparastes
options.note: MS1932; another verb (leaving, not thrusting away).

decisions.why: *contrítio* is *ruína* in 13:3 (the row, open), and the row itself says 59:4 will want another word: here the plural stands after *sana*, and the earth is healed of what the quake broke in it. The Greek is συντρίμματα, 'breakings, fractures' (the noun of συντρίβω = contérere). *fraturas* keeps the breaking and is what is healed; *brechas* is DRB's 'breaches' (a wall, not a body); *chagas* (MS1932) and *feridas* keep the healing but lose the breaking. 146:3 *álligat contritiónes eórum* (the broken-hearted) should weigh the same choice.

options.label: fraturas
options.note: Ruling; συντρίμματα, the thing broken, and a thing that is healed.

options.label: chagas
options.note: MS1932; the wound, without the breaking.

options.label: ruínas
options.note: the row's word (13:3); a ruin is not healed.

decisions.why: The colon closes on the verb that opened the verse (*Commovísti … commóta est*), and *abalar* (the *movéri / commovéri* row, 17:8, 45:7) is kept for both, so the echo stands. The perfect passive can be the event ('was shaken', ἐσαλεύθη aorist) or the state ('is shaken', MS1932 *está abalada*). The event is ruled: it points back to *Abalastes*, which is the Latin's repetition; the state stays an option.

The Latin word is *compúnctio*, the sting (L&S: 'a puncture … the sting of conscience'), which is the noun of 4:5 *compungímini → compungi-vos* (D8). The Greek behind it, κατάνυξις, is stupor, a wine that stuns; DRB 'wine of sorrow', MS1932 *vinho da amargura* — both give a sense, not the word. The Latin's word is kept (rule 1: the Latin as Latin), without the article, as the Latin (*a wine of*). Cost: *compunção* is a churchgoer's word, and the blind reader may not know it.

options.label: compunção
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's word, the family of 4:5 *compungi-vos*.

options.label: aturdimento
options.note: the Greek's sense (κατάνυξις, stupor); not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: *a fácie* (ἀπὸ προσώπου) after a verb of fleeing: the *a fácie* row gives *da face de* for *a fácie terræ* (1:4) and *diante de* where it is a cause (37:4) or a presence (60:4 *a fácie inimíci → diante do inimigo*). *Fugir de diante de* is the Portuguese for fleeing from before someone, keeps both prepositions (*a* + *fácies*), and is MS1932's wording (*de diante do arco*); DRB 'from before the bow'. *da face do arco* keeps the noun but makes a bow with a face. The colon is sung alone in the office of St Emygdius (Sancti/Urbis/08-09, grep).

options.label: de diante do
options.note: Ruling; MS1932, DRB; the row's *diante de* with the *a* of flight.

decisions.why: The Latin names no object: *salvum* is masculine singular, which points at the speaker (*et exáudi me* follows), but the sentence before speaks of *dilécti tui*, plural. DRB supplies 'me', MS1932 *salva-nos*; each decides. *Salvai com a vossa direita* keeps the Latin's openness and is sayable; the *me* of *escutai-me* then carries over, as in the Latin. *salvum fácere → salvar* (row). 107:7 has the same colon.

options.label: salvai
options.note: Ruling; no object, as the Latin.

decisions.why: The row *sancta / sanctum (a place) → o lugar santo* (19:3, 21:4, 23:3) names 59:8 as one of the places where *in sancto* 'is not always a place'. The Latin *sancto* can be the holy place or the holy one; the Greek ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ αὐτοῦ is the same neuter; the Hebrew's 'by his holiness' is not the Latin's. DRB 'in his holy place' and MS1932 *no seu santuário* both read a place. The row's wording is kept; *santuário* is kept for sanctuárium (72:17 …).

options.label: na sua santidade
options.note: the Hebrew's sense; not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: The Hebrew has a place name (Succoth); the Latin, following the Greek (τὴν κοιλάδα τῶν σκηνῶν), translates it: 'the vale of tents'. *tabernáculum → tenda* (row), so *o vale das tendas*. MS1932 capitalises *o vale dos Tabernáculos* as a name, which the Latin text does not do.

options.label: o vale dos tabernáculos
options.note: MS1932 (as a name); the row's option.

decisions.latin: Juda rex meus: * Moab olla spei meæ.
decisions.why: The Latin is verbless, carrying *est* over from 59:9 (*Meus est … meus est … et Éphraim fortitúdo*). Portuguese needs the copula to be heard as a sentence rather than a list, and D2 lets it be supplied; it is also supplied in 59:9's second colon (*e Efraim é a força*), where the Latin already lacks it. DRB and MS1932 supply it. The verbless build is the option.

options.label: Judá é o meu rei / Moab é

decisions.why: *olla* is a cooking pot (L&S; the Greek λέβης, a cauldron); the image is Moab as a menial vessel, and rule 5 keeps it concrete. *panela* is the plain word for it. MS1932 softens it (*como que o vaso*), and *vaso* is heard in Brazil as a flowerpot or worse. The twin 107:10 has another Latin word, *lebes*, for the same Greek; by D15's test it may take the same Portuguese, or *caldeirão* if Ps 107 wants to show the Latin's variation — proposed in the glossary as open.

*in* + accusative after a verb of stretching: over or into Edom (ἐπὶ τὴν Ιδουμαίαν). MS1932 *sobre a Idumeia*; DRB 'Into Edom'. *Sobre* keeps the gesture of possession the image makes (the shoe thrown or set over a land); *até a Idumeia* is 59:11's *usque in*, which the Latin keeps apart.

L&S: 'a covering for the foot, a shoe'. *calçado* is the generic word, as *calceaméntum* is, and is MS1932's; *sandália* names a kind the Latin does not name, though it is what the ear pictures in the Bible.

options.label: sandália
options.note: concrete, but a kind the Latin does not name.

decisions.why: The perfect passive states what is so (DRB 'are made subject'); ὑπετάγησαν. *ser sujeito a* is the row for *súbditus esse* (36:6), in the family of *sujeitar* (46:4). *a mim* stays first, as the Latin's *mihi*. *alienígenæ* (ἀλλόφυλοι) → *estrangeiros*, kept apart from *aliénus → estranho* (17:46); proposed in the glossary. 107:10 differs here (*amíci facti sunt*).

options.label: se sujeitaram
options.note: active reflexive; the Latin is passive.

decisions.latin: Quis dedúcet me … quis dedúcet me
decisions.why: *dedúcere, deduc me → guiar* is settled (D22; 5:9, 60:4 *Vós me guiastes*). Here the Greek varies (ἀπάξει … ὁδηγήσει) and the Latin repeats one verb; the repetition is kept. *conduzir* (MS1932) is natural for leading into a city and the future is outside the homograph ban, but it would break D22 in a verse where the Latin's verb is the row's own.

decisions.latin: Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos?
decisions.why: A verbless question answering 59:11's *Quis dedúcet me?*: 'Is it not you, God, who cast us off?' The copula must be supplied; the future *sereis* takes it from *dedúcet* (who will lead? — will it not be you), and keeps the Latin's paradox that the one who rejected is the one who leads. *Não sois vós* reads as a reproach only. MS1932 *Quem, senão tu* turns the question round and explains it. DRB 'Wilt not thou, O God'.

*de* here is 'out of' (ἐκ θλίψεως; DRB 'help from trouble'). *auxílio da tribulação* is heard as help that comes from the trouble. The *tribulátio* row has 31:7 *a tribulatióne → contra a tribulação*, which says help against it; MS1932 *na tribulação* moves the help into the trouble. Ruled for the row's precedent. The colon is a Matins antiphon (*Da nobis * Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne*, Psalmi matutinum, grep) and a versicle of a local office (08-SanteDultim).

options.label: para sair da tribulação
options.note: the sense of *de* spelled out; adds a verb.

decisions.why: The row *fácere virtútem → agir com poder* was written for this verse (117:16 *A direita do Senhor agiu com poder*; Ps 117's note: 'serves 59:14 too'). The singular *virtus* keeps *poder*, while 59:12's plural *virtútes nostræ* is *forças* (D43) — the cost the D43 ruling already accepted. MS1932 *faremos proezas* is the row's option.

choices.59:3: *irásci → irar-se*, *miseréri → ter piedade de* (rows). The Latin's two perfects, anger and mercy, are kept as the past (the Hebrew's imperative 'restore us' is not the Latin's). *et … et* kept as *e*; MS1932's *porém* interprets. Bare vocative *Deus*, as in the finished psalms; the pronoun *vós* supplied at the head (D2), as 60:4 *Vós me guiastes*.
choices.59:4: *commovére → abalar* (17:8, 45:7), *conturbáre → perturbar* (row), *sanáre → curar* (row; the row names 59:4).
choices.59:6: *metuéntes te* → *os que vos temem*: the same Greek (φοβούμενοι) as *timéntes te* (118:63 row). The verse ends on a colon because it runs on into 59:7 (*ut … ut*), and the Portuguese repeats *para que … Para que* as the Latin repeats *ut*.
choices.59:7: *liberáre → livrar* (row), passive *sejam livrados*. *dilécti tui → os vossos amados* (the *diléctus* row). *déxtera → a direita* (row). *exaudíre → escutar* (D3). 107:6b–7a has the same words and should copy them.
choices.59:8: *lætábor → eu me alegrarei*: the pronoun supplied (D2) so the colon does not open on a clitic and so that the oracle is heard to begin. *partíri → repartir* (= 21:18 *repartiram*, where the Latin is divídere; 107:8 *dívidam* is the same Greek, διαμεριῶ, and can copy it). *metíri → medir*. The Latin's second colon has an inner colon (*Síchimam:*), kept.
choices.59:9: *fortitúdo → força* (row). Names in their Vulgate-family Portuguese forms, as MS1932 prints them (Galaad, Manassés, Efraim, Judá, Moab, Idumeia, Siquém), not the Hebrew-based ones (Gileade). 107:9 differs here (*suscéptio*).
choices.59:11: *cívitas muníta → cidade fortificada* (row; the row names 59:11). *usque in → até*.
choices.59:12: The second colon is 43:10's word for word (*e não saireis, Deus, com as nossas forças*, D43), with the Latin's question mark; *virtútes nostræ → forças* (D43 names 59:12b).
choices.59:13: *quia vana salus hóminis → porque é vã a salvação do homem*: *salus → salvação* (D6); the copula supplied.
choices.59:14: *ad níhilum dedúcere → reduzir a nada* (row; names 59:14). *tribulántes nos → os que nos atribulam* (row; unknown to several blind readers, kept for the family of *tribulação* — and *tribulátio* stands in 59:13 just before). *ipse → ele mesmo* (MS1932), the emphasis kept.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal text for this psalm in the parallels file). Doublet (rule 6): 59:7–14 = 107:6b–14, and Ps 107 is not yet translated, so nothing to copy from it; Ps 56 overlaps 107:2–6 only, not this psalm. 59:12b copies 43:10b (D43). Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do/horas/Latin: the Matins antiphon *Da nobis * Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne* (Psalmi matutinum), versicles from 59:13 in a local office of Our Lady (aliquibus locis/08-SanteDultim), 59:6 in the office of St Emygdius (Urbis/08-09). Hard readings: 59:4 *contritiónes* (the row's *ruína* does not fit), 59:5 *vino compunctiónis* (the Latin's word against the Greek's stupor), 59:7 *salvum fac* with no object, 59:9b *olla*, 59:12 the verbless *Nonne tu*.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 59:3b +3 (elisions *piedade‿de*, not counted), 59:6a −5 (the Latin's long *significatiónem*), 59:7a +4 (*livrados*; *livres* would save one and blur the passive), 59:9b +6 (the copula and articles Portuguese needs against an 8-syllable verbless Latin; the verbless option is in `copula`), 59:12b −5 (43:10b's words, rule 6), 59:14b +4 (*ele mesmo* keeps *ipse*; elisions *reduzirá‿a*, *nada‿os*). All accepted. No cadence rhyme flagged.
